source.title: Disentangling Polysemantic Neurons with a Null-Calibrated Polysemanticity Index and Causal Patch Interventions

page_placements.theme: What units encode, and how polysemantic or describable they are, varies with depth (vision and audio classifiers; LM neuron roles in the original SoLU source)

record.tranche_reason: The study measures visual-neuron polysemanticity with a new quantitative index and prototype interventions, rather than reproducing the original qualitative feature-visualization method.
record.gate_note: The study reports PSI and component AUROCs against randomized null data, a layer-depth comparison, selected-neuron examples, patch-swap results, and measurement-sensitivity results. The discussion of prior work and superposition is not itself a result. The reported AUROC for PSI in layer4 conflicts: Table 1 gives 0.987, while the results text and Figure 2b give 0.599.
record.test_reason: It applies a new quantitative index (clustering of CLIP-embedded top patches) to an ImageNet-trained image classifier, ResNet-50, to identify neurons with distinct activation clusters. It also reports how that classification shifts with the scoring choices (top-K, text encoder). This bears on V1 and V7, with a different method from the original feature visualization.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude PSI separates real neurons from null (headlining AUROC ≈0.99), finds higher polysemanticity in layer4 than layer3, and that patch swaps confirm the prototypes' causal relevance. They call PSI rankings robust to hyperparameters, despite low K correlations, and name the text encoder as the larger sensitivity. They speculatively attribute the depth trend to superposition without testing it.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces a null-calibrated composite index using CLIP patch embeddings, clustering, class-label alignment, and open-vocabulary text distinctness, plus patch-swap interventions; it does not use the original qualitative feature-visualization procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: PSI ranking stability varies with the number of top patches K. D-score agreement varies with the CLIP text head (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.21). The paper also reports a difference between layer3 and layer4.

fits_no_version.finding: Index-measured polysemanticity is higher in deeper layers of a vision CNN (layer4 > layer3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision CNNs, the share or degree of polysemantic neurons increases with depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting a patch from a neuron's own prototype cluster at the peak site raises activation more than control patches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-cluster prototypes of a neuron are causally sufficient to drive it at the site.

record.problems: The layer4 full-PSI AUROC conflicts between Table 1 (0.987) and the results text/Figure 2b (0.599). Sensitivity results also give differing K-trend values in the prose and Appendix Figure 4 description. The intervention set is 10 selected high-PSI neurons, while the qualitative examples are selected channels; the text does not report numerical means or uncertainty bounds for individual control conditions. The study uses a single pretrained architecture and dataset for its main analysis.

untested.parts: InceptionV1 and the cat-face/car-front example; prevalence of polysemantic neurons (no share above a threshold reported).
All. Superposition is invoked only as speculation for the depth trend.
All: noise and regularization are mentioned only as cited prior work.
All: one architecture, no activation, regularizer or performance comparison.
All: the study does not examine whether a neuron's clusters reflect one shared feature.
Moderate-activation ranges are not examined (acknowledged as a limitation); other explanation-scoring methods are not compared.

missing.what: Qualitative depth contrast: top layer3 neurons respond to textures and patterns, top layer4 to object parts or whole objects.

record.verdict_notes: The AUROC rows are self-validation of the metric and are unlinked. The rotation null for S should preserve silhouette exactly, so Ŝ results are suspect. The paper has internal numeric inconsistencies: 0.987 vs 0.599, and 0.41 vs 0.42 at different K. The non-aligned-cluster patch decreasing activation is not discussed as tension with polysemanticity. Single model, preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 or the specific cat-face/car-front example; tests selected ResNet-50 channels on Tiny-ImageNet instead.
Language models, transformer MLP neurons, and token/context polysemanticity are not tested.
The paper discusses superposition but does not test whether capacity pressure causes the observed polysemanticity.
Does not test initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes, or whether polysemanticity occurs with sufficient capacity.
Uses one architecture and pretrained model; does not compare activation functions, architectures, or regularization, or measure performance costs of reducing polysemanticity.

Does not establish the prevalence of truly unrelated mixtures across neurons or revisit the canonical InceptionV1 example. It tests semantic separability in selected ResNet-50 channels, but does not establish that the distinct clusters are unrelated in the strong sense of the version.
Tests sensitivity to the number of top patches and to the text encoder; does not compare other activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared full PSI scores for real neuron activations with randomized null data.
rows.measure: AUROC for distinguishing real neurons from null neurons using full PSI
rows.uncertainty: Figure 2b shows a 95% bootstrap CI, but its numerical bounds are not stated.
rows.note: The paper gives conflicting AUROCs for layer4. The figure and prose call 0.599 the AUROC; Table 1 gives 0.987.
rows.check: Validates the metric against a randomized null; it does not measure neurons responding to unrelated inputs. The layer4 AUROC conflicts: Table 1 gives 0.987, while the prose and Fig 2b give 0.599.

rows.note: The paper describes Ŝ as semantically blind.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared PSI distributions across network depths.
rows.measure: PSI distribution and median by layer
rows.value: Layer4 distribution shifted to higher values; layer4 median exceeds the layer3 75th percentile; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test p ≪ 10⁻⁶
rows.note: The study reports a depth difference within the same model.
rows.check: Shows layer4 channels score higher on PSI than layer3, consistent with multi-cluster neurons in an image classifier. No share of polysemantic neurons or threshold is given. V6 link removed: the study does not ask whether the clusters share one feature.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, layer4 channel 1680
rows.operation_detail: Examined the top-activating patches and their clusters for a high-PSI channel.
rows.measure: Cluster composition and visual character of high-activation patches
rows.value: Two visually distinct clusters, approximately 54/46: vertical/column-like structures versus foliage/texture backgrounds
rows.note: The paper presents this as a high-PSI example; it does not quantify how often such neurons occur.
rows.check: One selected channel whose top patches split into unrelated-looking clusters (columns vs foliage). V6 link removed: the study does not test for a shared underlying feature.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, layer4 channel 1721
rows.operation_detail: Examined the top-activating patches and their clusters for a lower-PSI channel.
rows.measure: Visual coherence and semantic distinctness of high-activation patches
rows.value: Consistently responds to dog faces; minor pose/viewpoint subclusters; semantic distinctness D is low and overall PSI is lower
rows.note: The authors present this as a more monosemantic comparison channel.
rows.check: A monosemantic contrast example (dog faces); it does not bear on whether some neurons are polysemantic.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, 10 selected layer4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the peak-activating patch with an aligned patch from the same prototype cluster.
rows.measure: Change in target-site neuron activation, ΔAc
rows.value: Mean increase of +0.15 relative to the neuron’s typical activation range
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI shown in Figure 2d; numerical bounds not stated; paired t-test comparisons with controls p < 0.05
rows.note: The intervention tests whether a discovered prototype causally activates its corresponding neuron.
rows.check: The patch swap tests causal relevance of the study's own prototypes, not polysemanticity. The baseline is the peak patch, and 'relative to typical range' is undefined.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, 10 selected layer4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the peak-activating patch with a non-aligned prototype from another cluster of the same neuron.
rows.measure: Change in target-site neuron activation, ΔAc
rows.value: Significant decrease in activation; no increase comparable to aligned patches
rows.uncertainty: Paired t-test comparison with aligned condition p < 0.05
rows.note: No numerical mean or CI for this control is stated.
rows.check: A patch from the neuron's other cluster decreased activation, which sits oddly with the neuron being driven by both concepts. The control is relative to the peak patch, so it is not interpretable as evidence for or against V1.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, 10 selected layer4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the peak-activating patch with a patch from an unrelated neuron.
rows.measure: Change in target-site neuron activation, ΔAc
rows.value: Significant decrease in activation; no increase comparable to aligned patches
rows.uncertainty: Paired t-test comparison with aligned condition p < 0.05
rows.note: No numerical mean or CI for this control is stated.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, 10 selected layer4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Inserted an aligned patch at a different image location.
rows.measure: Change in activation at the original target site, ΔAc
rows.uncertainty: 95% CI shown in Figure 2d; numerical bounds not stated
rows.note: The authors use this as a spatial-location control.

rows.subject: ResNet-50, 10 selected layer4 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Modified a different image region instead of the target patch.
rows.measure: Change in target-site neuron activation, ΔAc
rows.value: Failed to produce an increase similar to the aligned condition; authors say this rules out generic image-modification effects
rows.uncertainty: Paired t-test comparisons with controls p < 0.05; no separate numerical value stated
rows.note: The control’s individual numerical mean is not stated.
rows.check: Method-validation control. No numeric value is given.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Counted the silhouette-selected optimal cluster count among high-PSI layer4 neurons.
rows.measure: Distribution of optimal cluster counts, K̂
rows.value: The vast majority are best described by 2 or 3 clusters; very few require 4 or 5
rows.note: Counts for the individual cluster numbers are not stated.
rows.check: The K̂ search range is 2–5, forcing at least 2 clusters, so the distribution cannot show whether a neuron is monosemantic. Counts are not given.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of top patches used to calculate PSI and compared neuron rankings with the K=50 baseline.
rows.measure: Spearman rank correlation of PSI neuron rankings
rows.value: Appendix Figure 4: correlation rises from approximately 0.21 at K=10 to 0.42 at K=40; §5.4 also says it increases from 0.41 at K=30 toward the K=50 baseline
rows.note: The paper says rankings remain sensitive to this hyperparameter; the prose and figure description give different values for the trend.
rows.check: Ranking correlation with the K=50 baseline is low (≈0.21 at K=10 to ≈0.42 at K=40), so which neurons rank as polysemantic depends strongly on how much of the top activation range is used. The prose claims robustness and gives 0.41 at K=30, which conflicts with Fig 4.

source_check.problem: Prose says 0.41 at K=30; caption says about 0.21 at K=10 and 0.42 at K=40. The row note already flags this.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed D scores using a different CLIP text head and compared scores across encoders.

conditions.value: default versus alternative CLIP text head

rows.baseline: D scores from the default text head
rows.value: ρ ≈ 0.21; described as a modest positive correlation with considerable variance
rows.note: The authors say semantic distinctness depends on the text encoder’s conceptual ontology.
rows.check: D scores under two CLIP text heads correlate only ρ≈0.21, so explanation scoring depends on the encoder.

relation.reason: Its own results on layer depth, K sensitivity and text-head sensitivity bear on V1 and V7.

tranche.reason: A new index (clustering plus CLIP scoring) applied to ResNet-50, aimed at the same question: which neurons have unrelated, multi-cluster top activations.

source_check.notes: The text contradicts itself. Layer4 full-PSI AUROC is 0.987 in Table 1 (the abstract and intro say about 0.99) but 0.599 in the §5.1 prose and Fig 2b. K-sensitivity is 0.41 at K=30 in the prose but about 0.42 at K=40 in the Fig 4 caption. The authors call the rankings robust despite these low correlations. Their superposition account of the depth trend is untested. The figures are missing from the text, so values come from prose and captions.
